subject: Data lifespan, deletion, and residency – hosted API details
messages:
From: Emma Frost <emma.frost@novara.health>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Novara Security <security@novara.health>
Date: 2026-08-20T08:15:00-04:00
Subject: Data residency, retention, and deletion for hosted API

Hi Sean —

Thanks for the quick intro yesterday. As we evaluate Redwood for our product pipeline, our security and privacy team asked for written confirmation on a few hosted-API specifics so we can complete the attached questionnaire (Novara_Security_Questionnaire_v3.pdf). Could you help confirm the following for hosted API customers in the EU region?

- Where customer request/response text is stored (region / logical partitioning)
- Default retention windows for request/response payloads, logs, and embeddings
- Deletion behavior: if Novara requests deletion of a tenant's dataset, how quickly is data removed from live storage and from backups/snapshots?
- Are short-term model caches or KV caches persisted to disk or retained beyond the immediate request?
- Any contractual language (SLA) or options for stricter retention/backups for regulated customers?

We want to align on exact timelines we can commit to in our procurement review. Happy to jump on a short call if that’s easier.

Thanks,
Emma Frost
Head of Security Operations
Novara Health

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Emma Frost <emma.frost@novara.health>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-20T09:02:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Data residency, retention, and deletion for hosted API

Emma — thanks for sending this over and for the clear list. I’ve attached a short SOC2 summary and a diagram of our hosted API data flows to help. I’m looping in Monica (security) for the technical retention/deletion specifics and Marcus (infra) for region/replication details.

At a high level:
- We operate EU-hosted tenants in EU regions (Azure/EU & GCP/EU zones) and partition customer data per-tenant.
- Default short-term request/response retention is intentionally limited; we surface APIs and contractual options to shorten/lengthen depending on commitments.
- Deletions via the API trigger removal from active stores quickly; backups have longer windows — Monica will provide exact windows and forensic details.

If helpful, we can convert the answers into a short mutual action plan and redlined clause you can share with procurement.

Attachments: redwood-soc2-summary.pdf, data-flow-hostedapi-diagram.png

— Sean
Sean Gallagher
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Emma Frost <emma.frost@novara.health>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-20T11:35:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Data residency, retention, and deletion for hosted API — technical answers

Emma / team — following up with specific, operational answers you can use in the questionnaire and procurement review. I kept to observable behaviors rather than contract language; Kimberly can propose precise wording for agreements.

1) Residency / partitioning- We host EU tenants in EU regions only when the tenant has selected EU residency; the control plane remains multi-region but metadata that identifies tenancy is sharded and access-restricted. For Novara we can pin your tenant to GCP-EU (e.g., europe-west1) or Azure EU regions.

2) Default retention windows (hosted API)
- Request/response payloads (full text): default 30 days from ingestion for customers on standard hosted plan. This includes text used for generation and chat histories stored to provide conversation continuity.
- Embeddings / vector indexes derived from customer data: default 90 days, unless explicitly configured to persist longer for application needs.
- Operational logs (routing, error traces): 90 days. We retain sanitized traces for debugging; full payloads are not retained in operational logs by default.
- Audit logs (who accessed control plane, config changes): 365 days (required for many enterprise audits).

3) Deletion behavior
- Customer-initiated delete (via API or console): we remove the data from primary/active stores within 24 hours; a deletion event is recorded in the tenant’s audit trail.- Backups & snapshots: we perform incremental backups; snapshots that include deleted data remain on backup media until rotated. By default we recommend a 30-day snapshot retention window for hosted tenants — in practice that means data may persist in backups up to 30 days after deletion. For enterprise contracts we can shorten this window (see contractual options).
- Replicas: if your tenant is pinned to a single EU region, replicas remain within the EU region. Deletions propagate to replicas within the same 24-hour window for active stores.

4) Short-term caches / KV caches / model caches
- Runtime KV / attention caches are ephemeral and live in GPU/memory. We do not persist these caches to long-term storage.- Some internal short-duration request caching (to reduce repeated prefix cost) is retained in an encrypted cache layer for up to 1 hour by default and is purged thereafter. These caches are not indexed for search.

5) GDPR / Right to Erasure
- We support customer requests for erasure and can supply proof-of-deletion events from audit logs. For end-user erasure requests where Novara acts as the data controller, Novara should submit the request through the tenant-level deletion API or request via support channels; we will process per the timelines above.

6) Exceptions / forensic copies
- If we need to retain copies for legal reasons (e.g., legal hold) we will notify the customer. We do not hold forensic copies beyond the periods above unless required by law.

7) Verification & evidence
- We can provide deletion events and relevant audit logs as part of SOC2 / contractual evidence (redacted as necessary).

If you need explicit shorter windows (e.g., immediate purge from backups within 7 days), we can include that as an obligation in a Data Processing Addendum or in the Dedicated / Private offer.

Links: https://redwood.app/docs/hosted-data-lifecycle

— Monica Patel
Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Emma Frost <emma.frost@novara.health>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-20T15:10:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Data lifespan, deletion, and residency – contractual notes

Emma — I’ve added a few contractual points / recommended DPA language you can propose to procurement. Short summary below; happy to draft redlines if needed.

- Residency commitment: Redwood will store and process Novara tenant data in EU region(s) agreed at onboarding. Any cross-border processing must be explicitly authorized.
- Active storage deletion SLA: Redwood will remove customer data from active production stores within 24 hours of a valid deletion request.
- Backup retention & purge: By default backups may retain deleted data for up to 30 days. For enterprise customers we can contractually commit to a shorter backup purge window (e.g., 7 or 14 days) and provide evidence of purge via audit logs.
- Evidence: Deletion events and associated audit logs will be made available under the DPA and can be delivered through a secure link for compliance reviewers.
- Escrow / legal hold: If Novara requires legal hold capability we can add a special process; this will be subject to separate agreement.

Next steps I suggest:
1) If Novara wants a contractual 14-day backup purge, confirm and we’ll prepare a DPA addendum.
2) If you’d like more granular retention (e.g., embeddings retained 7 days), outline the specific collections and we’ll produce a cost/ops impact note.

I’ll prepare short redline language for the 24-hour active deletion + 30-day backup default and include an optional 14-day backup clause.

— Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Liam O'Neal <liam.oneal@novara.health>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Emma Frost <emma.frost@novara.health>
Cc: Novara Security <security@novara.health>
Date: 2026-08-21T11:42:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Data lifespan, deletion, and residency – hosted API details

Thanks Sean / Monica / Kimberly — this is exactly what we needed. A couple quick clarifications before we loop procurement: 

- Can you confirm the 24-hour active deletion SLA applies to both request/response payloads and to derived artifacts (embeddings) if Novara requests full-tenant purge? (we note Monica’s default windows but want the deletion SLA to explicitly cover embeddings when a full purge is requested)
- For the optional 14-day backup purge, what is the timeline for Redwood to provide proof-of-purge once the window completes?

If you can confirm those two items, I’ll circulate internally and propose a short 30-minute call early next week to finalize the DPA addendum and sign-off. We’ll attach our completed questionnaire (see attached).

Thanks again —
Liam O’Neal
Vendor Risk Manager
Novara Health
